section_title: How can God understand what we cannot put into words?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 27 And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.

context_lines: This verse completes Paul’s explanation of the Spirit’s help in prayer. Verse 26 describes weakness and wordless groaning; verse 27 says that the God who searches hearts knows the Spirit’s mind.

The Spirit intercedes for the saints—God’s people—according to God’s will. The reason for confidence is the agreement between the Spirit’s work and God’s will, even when the person praying cannot see what should happen next.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly read this as assurance that God understands the Spirit’s intercession and that it accords with His will. The passage directs trust toward God’s understanding. It does not identify every desired outcome as something the Spirit must be requesting.
god_plan_lines: Paul also says in [Romans 8:34](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/8.htm) that the risen Christ intercedes for believers. Read together, the statements show God providing help through both the Son and the Spirit. The family relationship described earlier in the chapter includes help in the weakness of those who belong to Him.
current_position_lines: Our studies Prayer and Faith and What Does Prayer Look Like? understand these verses as an invitation to bring our weakness honestly before God. Prayer does not depend on perfectly formed requests. The Spirit helps where our understanding and words fall short, according to God’s will. We can trust Him without treating prayer as a way to secure a particular outcome.
